text:
alex: Hey — ran an nsys capture against the dedicated runtime to investigate the perf regression. The timeline shows a big GPU kernel hotspot but no source file/line info for our kernels, just hex addresses + jit symbols.

maria: Ugh. Are we shipping debug symbols in that image? which build variant did you use?

alex: It's the prod multi-stage image. Build stage generates .o with -g but the final stage copies binaries from /build/bin and strips them. I thought we used RelWithDebInfo... maybe a packaging step strips .debug.
sam: @alex can you paste the nsys command you used? also which container image tag?
alex: Sure:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,kernels,osrt -o /tmp/run.qdrep 
  docker run --gpus all --rm myorg/redwood-runtime:dedicated-2026-03 ./run_workload.sh
```
No extra LD_PRELOADs. Output has kernel names like `compiled_op_0` but no file:line.

jen: Two quick things we hit before: 1) CUPTI lib mismatch (driver vs container) can drop line info; 2) final-stage `strip --strip-debug` removes symbol tables. Also make sure binaries have Frame Pointer (fno-omit-frame-pointer) if you want decent unwinds.

maria: Also for CUDA/Nsys you often need CUPTI to be present at runtime in the container. Check `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` exists and is version-compatible with host driver. If it's missing, nsys will still capture kernels but can't resolve debug info.

sam: We have a helper script I pushed earlier: `tools/trace/fix-cupti.sh` that symlinks host cupti libs into the container. Try running with `--volume /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro` and set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

alex: Good tip, trying that now. One oddity: `nm -C bin/my_runtime | grep compiled_op` returns symbol names but `addr2line -e bin/my_runtime 0x7f4a3c` returns `??:0`. So symbol table exists but DWARF not found. Maybe .debug info is in separate files (.dwp) that weren't copied.

jen: Right — check `readelf --debug-dump=info bin/my_runtime` or `eu-readelf`. If the final image uses --strip-debug and stored debug info separately we need to bring the debug archives into the container or set `DEBUGINFOD_URLS` if using debuginfod.

trace-bot: perf-alert: kernel_latency spike detected at 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z (p50->p99 delta 4.3x). Related traces: /tmp/run.qdrep

maria: Another actionable: build with `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` AND remove any `strip` step in the container image. Or keep strip but copy `/usr/lib/debug` contents into the runtime image. Also add `-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fasynchronous-unwind-tables`.

sam: If you want a quick local repro without rebuilding: run the same binary from the build container (not the slim runtime) so debug files are present. i.e. `docker run --rm -it myorg/redwood-runtime:builder /build/bin/run_workload.sh` then profile that. If lines appear there, it's definitely packaging.

alex: Confirmed — running the builder image yields full file:line in nsys. So packaging step strips DWARF. Rebuilding with `RELWITHDEBINFO` and copying `*.debug` in final image fixed symbols.

jen: Nice. Follow-up: verify CUPTI match and run `nsys profile --export=sqlite,trace.db ...` then open in nsys-ui to check kernel-source correlation. Also validate driver versions with `nvidia-smi` on host vs `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` in container.

maria: FYI for future: add a CI job that does a quick `nsys` smoke on the final image to assert line info exists for a small kernel; catch this at build time.

alex: Will add an `eng-runtime` card. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
